title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: FLARE, Long-RAG & Other Advanced Patterns
summary: Beyond Self-RAG, CRAG, Agentic RAG, and RAG Fusion, several other advanced RAG patterns address specific limitations:

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body:
Beyond Self-RAG, CRAG, Agentic RAG, and RAG Fusion, several other advanced RAG patterns address specific limitations:

**FLARE (Forward-Looking Active Retrieval)** (Jiang et al., 2023): generates answers sentence by sentence. When the model is about to generate a sentence and the next token probability is below a threshold (uncertain), it uses that partial sentence as a retrieval query, fetches context, and then continues generation. Retrieval is triggered exactly when needed — eliminating unnecessary retrievals and enabling long-form generation that progressively retrieves.

**Long-RAG** (2024): instead of chunking, retrieves entire documents and uses an LLM with 128K+ context window. Works when the corpus is small enough (< 1,000 documents) that a few full documents fit in context. Eliminates chunk boundary issues.

**Speculative RAG** (Google, 2024): a small "drafter" LLM generates a fast speculative answer, a large "verifier" LLM checks and refines. Reduces latency by doing the cheap work first.

**Modular RAG**: assembles a RAG pipeline from interchangeable modules (router, retriever, memory, filter, generator) — each swappable independently. Every advanced RAG system is effectively a Modular RAG.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
ADVANCED RAG TECHNIQUES COMPARISON
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

FLARE (Forward-Looking Active Retrieval):
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "Explain transformer architecture and its applications in RAG"

Generate sentence 1: "Transformers use self-attention mechanisms..."
  Token probs: [0.95, 0.92, 0.88] → all high → no retrieval ✓

Generate sentence 2: "In RAG systems, the [UNCERTAIN: retrieval component works...]"
  Uncertainty detected! → Trigger retrieval
  Query: "retrieval component in RAG transformers"
  Retrieved: [chunk about bi-encoders, cross-encoders, FAISS]
  Regenerated: "In RAG systems, bi-encoders embed queries and docs..."

Generate sentence 3: "FAISS supports approximately [UNCERTAIN: N million vectors]"
  Uncertainty detected! → Trigger retrieval
  Query: "FAISS billion scale vector search"
  Retrieved: [FAISS documentation: supports 1B+ vectors]
  Regenerated: "FAISS supports 1 billion+ vectors using IVF indexing"

Result: Factual, specific answer with targeted retrieval ✓

CONTEXTUAL RAG (Anthropic):
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STANDARD CHUNK:
"The return window is 30 days from purchase date."
  Embedding: "return window 30 days purchase" ← lacks context

CONTEXTUAL CHUNK:
"[CONTEXT: This chunk is from the Returns & Refunds section 
of Acme Corp's Customer Policy manual. It describes the 
standard return window for physical product purchases.]
The return window is 30 days from purchase date."
  Embedding: richer representation → better retrieval for:
  "Acme return policy physical products" ✓
  "how long do I have to return something" ✓
  "customer rights purchase reversal" ✓

ADAPTIVE RAG ROUTING:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query → Fast Classifier (GPT-4o-mini, <100ms)
           │
           ├─ "What is 2+2?" → NO_RETRIEVAL → LLM direct (<300ms)
           │
           ├─ "What is the refund policy?" → SIMPLE_RAG 
           │   → single retrieval + generate (<1.5s)
           │
           └─ "Compare Q3 revenue to industry, citing our growth drivers"
               → COMPLEX_RAG → RAG Fusion + potentially Agentic RAG (<5s)

LATENCY + COST COMPARISON:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Strategy          P50 Latency   Cost/Query   Quality
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
No Retrieval      300ms         $0.003        Low (no docs)
Standard RAG      1.2s          $0.030        Good
RAG Fusion        2.5s          $0.080        Better
FLARE             3.0s          $0.100        Best (long-form)
Agentic RAG       6.0s          $0.150        Best (multi-step)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ADAPTIVE RAG routes 40% → no/simple, 45% → standard, 15% → complex
→ Blended cost: $0.042/query (vs $0.150 if always agentic)
→ Blended latency: ~2.0s P50 (vs ~6.0s if always agentic) ✓

LONG-RAG vs CHUNK-RAG:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
              CHUNK-RAG           LONG-RAG
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Corpus size   Any (millions)      < 1,000 docs
Retrieval     ANN similarity      Doc-level similarity
Context       5 chunks (~2K tok)  3-5 full docs (~30K tok)
Chunk issues  Yes (boundary)      None (full docs)
LLM needed    Standard 4K-8K     Long-context 128K+
Cost          Low                 High (long context)
Best for      Large corpora       Legal docs, technical manuals
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Use Long-RAG when: answers require reading entire documents,
corpus is small, boundary issues harm quality.
```

quiz.question: What is Speculative RAG and how does it reduce latency?
options: Each tool should return structured error strings (never raise exceptions that crash the agent).
Three guard rails: (1) Max iterations: StateGraph with iteration counter in state — if iteration > MAX_ITER, force-exit to generation; (2) Max tokens: track total tokens…
RRF implicitly deduplicates: if the same document appears in multiple ranked lists, it accumulates RRF score from all of them — resulting in a higher composite score.
Speculative RAG (Google Research, 2024) is analogous to speculative decoding: a small "drafter" LLM (GPT-4o-mini, Llama-8B) quickly generates a candidate answer from…
quiz.explanation: Speculative RAG (Google Research, 2024) is analogous to speculative decoding: a small "drafter" LLM (GPT-4o-mini, Llama-8B) quickly generates a candidate answer from retrieved context. A large "verifier" LLM (GPT-4o) only reads the drafter's answer + retrieved docs and decides: approve (return drafter answer) or refine (short correction).

quiz.question: What is Modular RAG and what modules does it define?
options: Formula: RRF_score(doc) = Σ 1/(k + rank_i) where k=60 (empirical constant, prevents top-ranked docs from dominating) and rank_i is the document's rank in the i-th result list.
Offline (rebuild): stop serving → re-index all documents → bring new index online.
RAG that handles non-text inputs: images, tables, audio, video.
Each module is independently replaceable — enabling systematic A/B testing.
quiz.explanation: Modular RAG (Gao et al., 2024 survey) defines six module types: (1) Indexing module: chunking strategy + embedding model; (2) Pre-retrieval module: query transformation (HyDE, multi-query, rewriting); (3) Retrieval module: retriever type (dense, sparse, hybrid) + K; (4) Post-retrieval module: reranking, contextual compression, context window management; (5) Generation module: LLM + prompt template + output parser;…

quiz.question: What is the difference between offline and online knowledge update strategies?
options: Graph RAG (Microsoft, 2024) builds a knowledge graph from the corpus: entities → nodes, relationships → edges.
Multi-query is more powerful (explores different semantic directions) but 3-5× more expensive.
Modern RAG (2023+): retriever is pre-trained independently (BEIR/MTEB), generator is a large instruction-tuned LLM, joint training is too expensive.
Offline (rebuild): stop serving → re-index all documents → bring new index online.
quiz.explanation: Offline (rebuild): stop serving → re-index all documents → bring new index online. Causes downtime. Online (incremental): upsert new document chunks to existing index without stopping serving.

quiz.question: What is RAPTOR and how does it improve hierarchical retrieval?
options: Graph RAG (Microsoft, 2024) builds a knowledge graph from the corpus: entities → nodes, relationships → edges.
Each module is independently replaceable — enabling systematic A/B testing.
Agentic RAG uses an LLM agent (LangGraph or ReAct-style) with tools including: vector search, web search, SQL queries, calculator, and code interpreter.
RAPTOR (Sarthi et al., 2024): recursively summarizes clusters of document chunks at multiple levels.
quiz.explanation: RAPTOR (Sarthi et al., 2024): recursively summarizes clusters of document chunks at multiple levels. Level 0: raw chunks. Level 1: cluster summaries (groups of related chunks).

quiz.question: What is Adaptive RAG?
options: RAG that handles non-text inputs: images, tables, audio, video.
Agentic RAG uses an LLM agent (LangGraph or ReAct-style) with tools including: vector search, web search, SQL queries, calculator, and code interpreter.
Standard RAG: ~5K input tokens (context + query) + ~500 output tokens = ~$0.03 per query (GPT-4o pricing).
Adaptive RAG (Jeong et al., 2024): a classifier (BERT-based, fast) categorizes the incoming query as: (1) no-retrieval needed (simple factual, LLM knows it); (2)…
quiz.explanation: Adaptive RAG (Jeong et al., 2024): a classifier (BERT-based, fast) categorizes the incoming query as: (1) no-retrieval needed (simple factual, LLM knows it); (2) single-step retrieval (standard RAG); (3) multi-step retrieval (agentic RAG). Routes each query to the appropriate pipeline. Trained on a labeled dataset of query difficulty.
